    cores: int | None = None,
    threads_per_run: int = DEFAULT_THREADS_PER_RUN,
    select_srx: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    original_srx: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    max_size: str | None = None,
    retries: int | None = None,
    backoff: float | None = None,
    keep_sra: bool = False,
    prefetch_only: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Download FASTQ for every run of every SRA experiment in this record.

    Lays the data out as ``<output_dir>/<accession>/<SRX>/<SRR>*.fastq.gz`` —
    one directory per experiment under a directory named for this record — via
    a Snakemake DAG (``prefetch → extract → compress``). Runs already marked
    done (a ``.<SRR>.success`` flag) are skipped, so this is safe to rerun on
    an unstable connection.

    Concurrency is resource-aware: at most ``ncbi_parallel`` runs ``prefetch``
    from NCBI at once (keeping the link busy without tripping throttling), while
    ``cores`` bounds total CPU across the local extraction/compression steps —
    so those two stages overlap instead of blocking each other.

    Pass ``select_srx`` to download only some of the record's experiments (see
    below).

    Parameters
    ----------
    output_dir : str or Path, default "."
        Parent directory; a ``<output_dir>/<accession>`` subtree is created for
        this record.
    ncbi_parallel : int, default :data:`DEFAULT_NCBI_PARALLEL`
        Maximum runs to ``prefetch`` (the NCBI network step) concurrently. Keep
        this modest to avoid NCBI throttling; it is independent of ``cores``.
    cores : int, optional
        Total CPU cores the DAG may use across all steps (defaults to the
        machine's CPU count). On an HPC allocation, pass the allotted cores
        (e.g. ``$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE``).
    threads_per_run : int, default :data:`DEFAULT_THREADS_PER_RUN`
        Threads handed to ``fasterq-dump``/``pigz`` for each run.
    select_srx : iterable of str, optional
        A whitelist of SRA experiment accessions (``SRX…``). When given, only
        the record's experiments whose accession is listed are downloaded and
        every other experiment is skipped; ``None`` (the default) downloads
        them all. Entries are matched case-insensitively and every one must be
        a well-formed ``SRX`` accession — anything else raises
        :class:`~labdata.exceptions.AccessionError`.
    original_srx : iterable of str, optional
        A set of SRA experiment accessions (``SRX…``) to fetch in *original
        format* instead of the default sra-tools path: every run of a listed
        experiment has its submitter-uploaded files downloaded as-is (no
        ``fasterq-dump``/gzip), because its ``.sra`` is missing or useless
        (e.g. a 10X run whose ``.sra`` stored only one read). This selects the
        *mode*; it does not by itself widen the selection — an experiment must
        still survive ``select_srx`` to be downloaded at all. Each entry must
        be a well-formed ``SRX`` accession or :class:`~labdata.exceptions.AccessionError`
        is raised.
    max_size : str, optional
        Passed to ``prefetch --max-size`` (defaults to :data:`DEFAULT_MAX_SIZE`);
        raise it for runs that exceed ``prefetch``'s 20G default.
    retries : int, optional
        Attempts for the resumable ``prefetch`` network step per run (defaults
        to :data:`DEFAULT_RETRIES`).
    backoff : float, optional
        Base seconds for the linear backoff between ``prefetch`` retries
        (defaults to :data:`DEFAULT_BACKOFF`).
    keep_sra : bool, default False
        Keep each run's downloaded ``.sra`` next to its FASTQ (as
        ``<accession>/<SRX>/<SRR>.sra``) instead of deleting it after extraction.
    prefetch_only : bool, default False
        Only ``prefetch`` each run's ``.sra`` (into ``<SRX>/<SRR>/``), skipping
        ``fasterq-dump``, gzip, and cleanup. A later full download resumes from
        extraction without re-fetching.
    verbose : bool, default True
        Print a download plan up front and one line per finished run to
        ``stderr``. Set ``False`` to download silently.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, bool]
        Maps each run accession to whether its data is present on completion.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> Series("GSE229022").download("./fastq", ncbi_parallel=3, cores=16)  # doctest: +SKIP
    {'SRR24084454': True, 'SRR24084455': True, ...}
    >>> BioProject("PRJNA1027859").download("./fastq", ncbi_parallel=3)  # doctest: +SKIP
    {'SRR26452081': True, 'SRR26452082': True, ...}
    >>> Series("GSE229022").download("./fastq", select_srx=["SRX19885398"])  # doctest: +SKIP
    {'SRR24084454': True}
    """
    # ``None`` overrides fall through to the sra-tools defaults.
    overrides = {
        key: value
        for key, value in {"max_size": max_size, "retries": retries, "backoff": backoff}.items()
        if value is not None
    }
    # Original-format experiments select the download *mode*, not the selection.
    original_set = _validate_srx_whitelist(original_srx, field="original_srx")
    base = Path(output_dir) / self.accession
    tasks: list[tuple[Run, Path]] = []
    original: set[str] = set()
    for experiment in self._selected_experiments(select_srx):
        srx_dir = base / experiment.accession
        srx_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        is_original = experiment.accession in original_set
        for run in experiment.runs:
            tasks.append((run, srx_dir))
            if is_original:
                original.add(run.accession)
    return _run_plan(
        self.accession,
        tasks,
        output_root=base,
        verbose=verbose,
        ncbi_parallel=ncbi_parallel,
        cores=cores,
        threads_per_run=threads_per_run,
        keep_sra=keep_sra,
        prefetch_only=prefetch_only,
        original=original,
        **overrides,
    )

bamtofastq ¶

Per-run cellranger-BAM → FASTQ stage behind the Snakemake tenx DAG.

This is a 10x-specific counterpart to :mod:labdata.geo.sratools. When a 10x run's SRA-normalized .sra is broken (e.g. it dropped the technical reads, leaving only R1), the usable source is the submitter's original cellranger BAM, which :mod:labdata.geo can fetch with the original-format download path. Turning that BAM back into correctly-split FASTQ requires 10x Genomics' own bamtofastq — a generic BAM→FASTQ tool cannot decode the 10x tags / @RG headers that separate the barcode (R1), cDNA (R2), and index (I1) reads, and would corrupt the read structure for a downstream STARsolo remap.

Every subprocess call is funnelled through the single :func:_run helper — the one place tests monkeypatch — so the stage (BAM discovery, the tool call, flattening its nested output into the download-style layout) is exercised without the bamtofastq binary. Orchestration — scheduling this stage across many runs — lives in :mod:labdata.tenx.pipeline (Snakemake); :class:TenxConverter drives that DAG over a whole :class:~labdata.geo.geo_records.Series or :class:~labdata.geo.bio_project_records.BioProject, auto-detecting which runs carry a 10x BAM.

def convert(
    self,
    *,
    cores: int | None = None,
    threads_per_run: int = DEFAULT_THREADS_PER_RUN,
    reads_per_fastq: int = DEFAULT_READS_PER_FASTQ,
    select_srx: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    all_runs: bool = False,
    from_disk: bool = False,
    remove_bam: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Convert every 10x-BAM run of this record's experiments to FASTQ.

    Auto-detects which runs carry a cellranger BAM (:func:`is_tenx_bam_run`) and
    converts each via a Snakemake DAG, laying the FASTQ out as
    ``<output_dir>/<accession>/<SRX>/<SRR>_S1_L00N_R{1,2}_00N.fastq.gz``. Runs
    already marked done (a ``.<SRR>.tenx.done`` marker) are skipped, so this is safe
    to rerun.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cores : int, optional
        Total CPU cores the DAG may use (defaults to the machine's CPU count). On an
        HPC allocation, pass the allotted cores (e.g. ``$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE``).
    threads_per_run : int, default :data:`DEFAULT_THREADS_PER_RUN`
        Threads handed to ``bamtofastq`` per run (``--nthreads``).
    reads_per_fastq : int, default :data:`DEFAULT_READS_PER_FASTQ`
        Reads per output FASTQ chunk (``bamtofastq --reads-per-fastq``).
    select_srx : iterable of str, optional
        A whitelist of SRA experiment accessions (``SRX…``). When given, only those
        experiments are considered; ``None`` (the default) considers them all. Each
        entry must be a well-formed ``SRX`` accession or :class:`AccessionError` is
        raised.
    all_runs : bool, default False
        Convert every run of the selected experiments, skipping the 10x-BAM
        auto-detection. Use when you know all runs carry a cellranger BAM (e.g. to
        avoid the extra SDL lookups) or to force conversion of a run SDL does not
        flag.
    from_disk : bool, default False
        Build the task list by scanning the on-disk tree
        (``<output_dir>/<accession>/<SRX>/<SRR>_*.bam``) instead of resolving the
        record through NCBI. This needs no network or NCBI credentials — the point
        when converting already-downloaded BAMs on an offline HPC compute node.
        ``select_srx`` still filters by experiment; ``all_runs`` and the SDL
        auto-detection do not apply (a BAM's presence on disk is the signal).
    remove_bam : bool, default False
        Delete each run's source BAM once its FASTQ are produced, reclaiming the
        large original. Deletion happens only after a run converts successfully.
    verbose : bool, default True
        Print a conversion plan up front and a summary to ``stderr``. Set ``False``
        to run silently.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, bool]
        Maps each converted run accession to whether its FASTQ are present on
        completion (empty if there are no 10x-BAM runs).
    """
    base = self.output_dir / self.record.accession
    if from_disk:
        tasks = _tasks_from_disk(base, _validate_srx_whitelist(select_srx))
    else:
        tasks = [
            (run, base / experiment.accession)
            for experiment in self._selected_experiments(select_srx)
            for run in experiment.runs
            if all_runs or is_tenx_bam_run(run)
        ]
    for srx_dir in {srx_dir for _, srx_dir in tasks}:
        srx_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return _run_conversion(
        self.record.accession,
        tasks,
        output_root=base,
        cores=cores,
        threads_per_run=threads_per_run,
        reads_per_fastq=reads_per_fastq,
        remove_bam=remove_bam,
        verbose=verbose,
    )

def is_tenx_bam_run(run: Run) -> bool:
    """Return whether ``run`` has an original-format 10x cellranger BAM.

    Inspects the run's original/submitted files (via the SRA Data Locator) for a BAM:
    an entry whose SDL type is ``TenX``/``bam`` or whose name ends in ``.bam``. This is
    the signal that the run should be recovered from its cellranger BAM rather than the
    (possibly broken) SRA archive — the runs :class:`TenxConverter` selects by default.

    Parameters
    ----------
    run : Run
        The SRA run to inspect.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        ``True`` if the run lists an original-format BAM, else ``False``.
    """
    return any(
        file.type.lower() in {"tenx", "bam"} or file.name.lower().endswith(".bam")
        for file in run.original_files
    )

def bamtofastq_run(
    run: Run,
    srx_dir: Path,
    *,
    threads: int = DEFAULT_THREADS_PER_RUN,
    reads_per_fastq: int = DEFAULT_READS_PER_FASTQ,
    remove_bam: bool = False,
) -> list[Path]:
    """Convert one run's on-disk cellranger BAM to FASTQ with ``bamtofastq``.

    The single stage of the tenx DAG. Locates the run's original-format BAM
    (``<srx_dir>/<SRR>_*.bam``), runs 10x's ``bamtofastq`` into a scratch dir, then
    flattens that nested output into ``<srx_dir>/<SRR>_S1_L00N_R{1,2}_00N.fastq.gz`` (see
    :func:`_flatten_output`) and removes the scratch. Idempotent: a stale scratch from
    an interrupted run is cleared first (``bamtofastq`` refuses a pre-existing output
    dir), so a rerun reconverts cleanly.

    Parameters
    ----------
    run : Run
        The run whose BAM to convert.
    srx_dir : Path
        The experiment directory holding ``<SRR>_<name>.bam``; the FASTQ land here.
    threads : int, default :data:`DEFAULT_THREADS_PER_RUN`
        Threads passed to ``bamtofastq --nthreads``.
    reads_per_fastq : int, default :data:`DEFAULT_READS_PER_FASTQ`
        Reads per output chunk (``bamtofastq --reads-per-fastq``).
    remove_bam : bool, default False
        Delete the source BAM once the FASTQ are produced. The deletion happens only
        *after* a successful conversion, so an interrupted run leaves the BAM in place
        for a resumed rerun to reconvert from.

    Returns
    -------
    list of Path
        The converted FASTQ files written under ``srx_dir``.

    Raises
    ------
    DownloadError
        If the BAM is missing/ambiguous, ``bamtofastq`` is missing or fails, or it
        produced no FASTQ (a non-original BAM).
    """
    accession = run.accession
    bam = _find_bam(srx_dir, accession)
    scratch = _scratch_dir(srx_dir, accession)
    if scratch.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(scratch)  # bamtofastq refuses an existing output dir
    _run(
        [
            "bamtofastq",
            f"--nthreads={threads}",
            f"--reads-per-fastq={reads_per_fastq}",
            str(bam),
            str(scratch),
        ]
    )
    moved = _flatten_output(scratch, srx_dir, accession)
    shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
    if remove_bam:
        bam.unlink(missing_ok=True)  # only reached on success — the FASTQ now stand in
    logger.info("converted %s (%d FASTQ)", accession, len(moved))
    return moved

entrez ¶

The one seam for NCBI E-utilities and the GEO download site.

Every NCBI call in liulab-data goes through :class:EntrezClient. E-utilities calls are POSTs over kept-open connections, paced by one limiter per process; Biopython's :func:Bio.Entrez.read parses the XML replies. fetch_text and download GET pages and files outside E-utilities. Every request has a socket timeout and is retried with jittered backoff when the failure is transient.

Responses are memoized per client instance, except efetch_records, download and stream, which bulk runs use.

def __init__(
    self,
    credentials: NcbiCredentials | None = None,
    *,
    allow_prompt: bool = True,
    transport: Transport | None = None,
    limiter: RateLimiter | None = None,
) -> None:
    self.credentials = credentials or load_credentials(allow_prompt=allow_prompt)
    self._transport: Transport = transport or HttpTransport()
    self._limiter = limiter or EUTILS_LIMITER
    self._identity = {"tool": _TOOL, "email": self.credentials.email}
    if self.credentials.api_key:
        self._identity["api_key"] = self.credentials.api_key
    else:
        self._limiter.lower_to(_KEYLESS_RATE)
    # Per-instance response cache keyed by call signature. Redundant lookups
    # across records that share this client are served without a request.
    self._cache: dict[tuple[Any, ...], Any] = {}

    if cached is None:

        docsums = _docsums(record)

        cached = self._cache[key] = dict(docsums[0])
    return cached

def esummary_many(self, db: str, uids: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Fetch document summaries for several UIDs in a single request.

    Collapses what would otherwise be one ESummary per UID into one batched
    call (NCBI accepts a comma-joined id list), chunked to keep the request
    URL within limits. Use this instead of looping over :meth:`esummary`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    db : str
        Entrez database (e.g. ``"gds"``, ``"sra"``, or ``"bioproject"``).
    uids : list of str
        The UIDs whose summaries to fetch. An empty list issues no request.

    Returns
    -------
    list of dict
        One document summary per UID, in NCBI's order. The mappings may carry
        NCBI's ``Id``/``uid`` so callers can recover each summary's UID via
        :func:`docsum_uid`. Cached per client by the exact UID list.
    """
    ids = [str(uid) for uid in uids]
    if not ids:
        return []
    key = ("esummary_many", db, tuple(ids))
    cached = self._cache.get(key)
    if cached is None:
        docsums: list[Any] = []
        for chunk in _chunked(ids, _ESUMMARY_CHUNK):
            record = self._eutil("esummary", {"db": db, "id": ",".join(chunk)})
            docsums.extend(_docsums(record))
        cached = self._cache[key] = docsums
    return list(cached)

def elink_many(self, dbfrom: str, db: str, uids: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Map each of several UIDs to the UIDs it links to, one request per chunk.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dbfrom : str
        Source database (e.g. ``"gds"``).
    db : str
        Target database (e.g. ``"sra"``).
    uids : list of str
        The source UIDs. An empty list issues no request.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to list of str
        Each distinct source UID mapped to its linked UIDs (empty if none).
    """
    wanted = list(dict.fromkeys(str(uid) for uid in uids))
    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {uid: [] for uid in wanted}
    for start in range(0, len(wanted), _ESUMMARY_CHUNK):
        chunk = wanted[start : start + _ESUMMARY_CHUNK]
        # A list ``id`` is sent as repeated parameters, so NCBI answers one set per UID.
        record = self._eutil("elink", {"dbfrom": dbfrom, "db": db, "id": chunk})
        for linkset in record:
            source = str((linkset.get("IdList") or [""])[0])
            for linksetdb in linkset.get("LinkSetDb", []):
                out.setdefault(source, []).extend(
                    str(link["Id"]) for link in linksetdb.get("Link", [])
                )
    return out

def efetch(
    self,
    db: str,
    ids: list[str],
    *,
    rettype: str,
    retmode: str = "text",
    refresh: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Fetch raw records via EFetch and return the response as text.

    Unlike the other helpers this returns the response **unparsed** (e.g. the
    SRA ``runinfo`` CSV), because EFetch serves formats Biopython does not
    parse into Python structures.

    Parameters
    ----------
    db : str
        Entrez database (e.g. ``"sra"``).
    ids : list of str
        The UIDs to fetch. An empty list issues no request.
    rettype : str
        EFetch return type (e.g. ``"runinfo"``).
    retmode : str
        EFetch return mode (default ``"text"``).
    refresh : bool
        Skip the cached response and request again (the new response is cached).

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The raw response body (empty string for an empty ``ids``). Cached per
        client by the exact request.
    """
    uids = [str(uid) for uid in ids]
    if not uids:
        return ""
    key = ("efetch", db, tuple(uids), rettype, retmode)
    cached = None if refresh else self._cache.get(key)
    if cached is None:
        params = {"db": db, "id": ",".join(uids), "rettype": rettype, "retmode": retmode}
        cached = self._cache[key] = self._eutil("efetch", params, _read_text)
    return cached

def efetch_records(
    self,
    db: str,
    ids: list[str],
    *,
    rettype: str,
    retmode: str = "xml",
    split: Callable[[str], Mapping[str, str]],
) -> FetchedRecords:
    """Fetch one batch of records, re-asking once for the ids the reply left out.

    NCBI can leave records out of a batch with no error; those ids are asked for again
    together. An "ID list is empty" answer marks the ids it covers missing and is not
    retried. A failed re-ask never drops what the batch already returned. Nothing is
    cached.

    Parameters
    ----------
    db : str
        Entrez database (e.g. ``"sra"``).
    ids : list of str
        The ids to fetch in one request.
    rettype : str
        EFetch return type (e.g. ``"full"``).
    retmode : str
        EFetch return mode (default ``"xml"``).
    split : callable
        Maps a reply's text to ``{id: record text}``, keyed as ``ids`` are.

    Returns
    -------
    FetchedRecords
        The records got, the ids NCBI has none for, and the ids whose re-ask failed.

    Raises
    ------
    EntrezError
        If the first request fails for a reason other than "ID list is empty".
    """
    out = FetchedRecords()
    todo = list(dict.fromkeys(str(i) for i in ids))
    for ask in range(2):
        params = {"db": db, "id": ",".join(todo), "rettype": rettype, "retmode": retmode}
        try:
            reply = self._eutil("efetch", params, _read_text)
        except EntrezError as err:
            if _ids_empty(err.__cause__ or err):
                out.missing = todo
            elif ask == 0:
                raise
            else:
                out.failed = dict.fromkeys(todo, str(err))
            return out
        asked = set(todo)
        out.records |= {k: v for k, v in split(reply).items() if k in asked}
        todo = [i for i in todo if i not in out.records]
        if not todo:
            break
    out.missing = todo
    return out

def download(self, url: str, dest: Path) -> int:
    """Stream a file from the GEO site to ``dest`` as it arrives, never whole in memory.

    The bytes are written as served (a ``.gz`` stays compressed) to a temporary file
    beside ``dest`` and renamed into place once complete.

    Parameters
    ----------
    url : str
        The file URL.
    dest : Path
        Where to write it.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Bytes written.

    Raises
    ------
    PageNotFound
        If the server answers 404.
    EntrezError
        If the request fails after the transient-failure retries.
    """
    part = dest.with_name(dest.name + ".part")

    def write(response: Response) -> int:
        size = 0
        with part.open("wb") as fh:
            while chunk := response.read(_CHUNK_BYTES):
                fh.write(chunk)
                size += len(chunk)
        return size

    try:
        size = self._get(url, write)
    except BaseException:
        part.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
    part.replace(dest)
    return size

def stream(
    self, url: str, consume: Callable[[Iterator[bytes]], _T], *, tries: int = _MAX_TRIES
) -> _T:
    """GET a file from the GEO site and hand its bytes to ``consume`` as they arrive.

    A gzip body is decompressed on the way. The body is read in chunks, so a large file
    is never whole in memory unless ``consume`` keeps it. Nothing is cached.

    Parameters
    ----------
    url : str
        The file URL.
    consume : callable
        Takes an iterator over the body's chunks, decompressed, and returns the result.
        It runs again from the start on each retry.
    tries : int
        Tries before giving up; ``1`` leaves retries and backoff to the caller.

    Returns
    -------
    object
        What ``consume`` returned.

    Raises
    ------
    PageNotFound
        If the server answers 404.
    EntrezError
        If the request fails ``tries`` times; the last failure is its ``__cause__``.
    """

    def read(response: Response) -> _T:
        body = io.BufferedReader(_RawBody(response), _CHUNK_BYTES)
        data: io.BufferedIOBase = body
        if body.peek(2)[:2] == b"\x1f\x8b":
            data = gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=body)
        result = consume(iter(lambda: data.read(_CHUNK_BYTES), b""))
        while body.read(_CHUNK_BYTES):  # drain, so the connection can be reused
            pass
        return result

    return self._get(url, read, tries=tries)

def retry_after(err: BaseException) -> float:
    """Return the seconds a throttled reply asked us to wait, or zero."""
    headers = getattr(err, "headers", None)
    value = headers.get("Retry-After") if headers is not None else None
    with contextlib.suppress(TypeError, ValueError):
        return max(0.0, float(value))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return 0.0

def docsum_uid(docsum: Any) -> str | None:
    """Return the NCBI UID of a single document summary, if present.

    Classic ``DocSum`` records (``gds``/``sra``) carry the UID under the ``Id``
    key; v2.0 ``DocumentSummary`` records (``bioproject``) carry it as the XML
    ``uid`` attribute, which Biopython exposes via ``.attributes``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    docsum : Any
        One summary from :meth:`EntrezClient.esummary_many`.

    Returns
    -------
    str or None
        The UID, or ``None`` when the summary carries none.
    """
    uid = docsum.get("Id") if hasattr(docsum, "get") else None
    if not uid:
        attributes = getattr(docsum, "attributes", None) or {}
        uid = attributes.get("uid")
    return str(uid) if uid else None

sdl ¶

A thin, mockable client for NCBI's SRA Data Locator (SDL).

The SRA Run Browser's "Data access" panel — both the normalized SRA archive files and the original format files the submitter uploaded — is served by the SDL service rather than by E-utilities. :class:SdlClient wraps the public sdl/2/retrieve endpoint and returns the file listing as plain :class:RemoteFile objects, so the rest of the package can discover (for example) the original 10X Genomics BAM behind a run whose .sra only stored one read.

Concentrating this network access in one seam keeps callers easy to unit-test by substituting a fake client, mirroring :class:labdata.ncbi.entrez.EntrezClient. Responses are memoized per client instance, keyed by accession.

def retrieve(self, accession: str) -> list[RemoteFile]:
    """Return every file SDL lists for ``accession``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    accession : str
        An SRA run accession, e.g. ``"SRR20172067"``.

    Returns
    -------
    list of RemoteFile
        Both the normalized SRA archive file(s) and any original/submitted
        files (e.g. a 10X ``possorted_genome_bam``). Cached per client.

    Raises
    ------
    SdlError
        If the request fails, the response is not valid JSON, or SDL reports a
        non-OK status for the accession (e.g. unknown or non-public run).
    """
    cached = self._cache.get(accession)
    if cached is None:
        payload = self._fetch(accession)
        cached = self._cache[accession] = _parse_files(payload, accession)
    return list(cached)

config ¶

NCBI E-utilities credential resolution.

NCBI asks every E-utilities client to identify itself with an email address, and optionally accepts an API key that raises the rate limit from 3 to 10 requests per second. This module resolves those two values from, in order:

  1. the NCBI_EMAIL / NCBI_API_KEY environment variables;
  2. a cached config file at <cache>/ncbi.toml;
  3. an interactive prompt (only on a TTY), whose answers are then cached.

In a non-interactive context with nothing configured, :func:load_credentials raises :class:CredentialsError with an actionable message rather than hanging.

def load_credentials(*, allow_prompt: bool = True) -> NcbiCredentials:
    """Resolve NCBI credentials from env vars, the cache file, or a prompt.

    Parameters
    ----------
    allow_prompt : bool
        When ``True`` (default) and nothing is configured, prompt interactively
        on a TTY and cache the answers. When ``False``, never prompt.

    Returns
    -------
    NcbiCredentials
        The resolved credentials.

    Raises
    ------
    CredentialsError
        If no credentials are configured and prompting is disabled or impossible
        (e.g. a non-interactive process).
    """
    creds = _from_env() or _from_file()
    if creds is not None:
        return creds

    if allow_prompt and _is_interactive():
        return prompt_and_save()

    raise CredentialsError(
        f"no NCBI credentials found. Set the {EMAIL_ENV} environment variable "
        f"(and optionally {API_KEY_ENV}), or run `labdata ncbi configure`."
    )

def open_many(self, accessions: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, Record | LabdataError]:
    """Open many records: one record lookup and one link lookup for the whole batch.

    Parameters
    ----------
    accessions : iterable of str
        Public accessions of any record type.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Each accession, in input order, mapped to its ``Record`` or to the error that
        stopped it (``AccessionError``, ``NotMirrored`` or ``NotFound``).
    """
    order = [_norm(a) for a in accessions]
    out: dict[str, Record | LabdataError] = {}
    valid: list[str] = []
    for accession in order:
        try:
            kind = kind_of(accession)
            if kind == PAPER:
                raise AccessionError(f"{accession} is a paper, not a record; follow 'PubMed'")
            if kind == ANNOTATION:
                raise AccessionError(
                    f"{accession} is a GEO named annotation, not a record; "
                    "follow 'Named Annotation'"
                )
            valid.append(accession)
        except AccessionError as err:
            out[accession] = err
    records = self.reader.records(valid) if valid else {}
    by_end = self._links(records) if records else {}
    absent = self._absent_errors(set(valid) - set(records))
    for accession in valid:
        record = records.get(accession)
        out[accession] = (
            absent[accession]
            if record is None
            else replace(record, links=tuple(by_end[accession]))
        )
    return {a: out[a] for a in order}

def links(
    self, accessions: str | Iterable[str], relation: str | None = None
) -> dict[str, list[Link]]:
    """Map each accession to its link rows as read from its end, in one reader call.

    A far end may be an accession the store does not hold.

    Parameters
    ----------
    accessions : str or iterable of str
        Accessions of any record type, or ``PMID:<n>``.
    relation : str or None
        Keep only links of this name as read from the given end, forward or reverse.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Each accession, in input order, mapped to its links sorted by relation, far end
        and source.

    Raises
    ------
    AccessionError
        If an accession is malformed.
    ValueError
        If the relation name is unknown.
    """
    accs = _accessions(accessions)
    relations = None if relation is None else [forward_name(relation)]
    found = self._links(set(accs), relations)
    return {
        a: [k for k in found[a] if relation is None or k.relation == relation] for a in accs
    }

    wanted = set(_accessions(accessions))
    texts = self.reader.raw(wanted) if wanted else {}
    self._raise_absent(wanted - set(texts))
    return dict(sorted(texts.items()))

    """Map each accession to the supplementary files its SOFT lists, in two reader calls.

    A Series lists its own files; its samples' files are under the samples. An

    dict

    ------
    AccessionError
        If an accession is malformed.
    NotMirrored
        If a snapshot lists an accession the store does not hold. The message lists
        every such accession.
    NotFound
        If no snapshot lists an accession. The message gives the snapshot date.
    """
    order = _accessions(accessions)
    self._require_held(set(order))
    out: dict[str, list[SupplementaryFile]] = {a: [] for a in order}
    for file in self.reader.supplementary_files(set(order)) if order else []:
        out[file.owner].append(file)
    return out

def experiments_for_many(
    self, accessions: Iterable[str], *, partial: bool = False
) -> dict[str, list[Experiment]] | Partial[dict[str, list[Experiment]]]:
    """Map each accession to the SRA experiments under it, built from stored packages.

    Walks down one level at a time, with one link lookup and one holdings lookup per
    level for all roots together.

    Parameters
    ----------
    accessions : iterable of str
        The roots of the walk.
    partial : bool
        Return what is held instead of raising ``NotMirrored``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict or Partial
        Each root mapped to its sorted experiments. With ``partial=True``, a ``Partial``
        whose ``held`` is that mapping over held records and whose ``missing`` lists every
        accession the walk reached but the store does not hold.

    Raises
    ------
    AccessionError
        If an accession is malformed.
    NotFound
        If no snapshot lists a root, even with ``partial``.
    NotMirrored
        If a root or a record on the way down is not held, unless ``partial``. The
        message lists every missing accession.
    """
    roots = _accessions(accessions)
    missing = self._require_held(set(roots), not_held_ok=True)
    found: dict[str, set[str]] = {r: set() for r in roots}
    level = {(r, r) for r in roots if r not in missing}
    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    while level:
        seen |= level
        todo = set()
        for root, acc in level:
            if kind_of(acc) == "SRA experiment":
                found[root].add(acc)
            else:
                todo.add((root, acc))
        if not todo:
            break
        children: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
        for row in self.reader.links({acc for _, acc in todo}):
            for end, link in _ends(row):
                if _leads_down(kind_of(end), link):
                    children.setdefault(end, set()).add(link.other)
        reached = {c for cs in children.values() for c in cs}
        held = self.reader.held(reached) if reached else set()
        missing |= reached - held
        level = {
            (root, child)
            for root, acc in todo
            for child in children.get(acc, ())
            if child in held
        } - seen
    if missing and not partial:
        raise NotMirrored(f"not held in this store: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}")
    wanted = {acc for accs in found.values() for acc in accs}
    packages = self.reader.raw(wanted) if wanted else {}
    built = {
        experiment.accession: experiment
        for experiment in experiments_from_package_xml(
            "".join(text.text for text in packages.values()),
            client=OfflineEntrezClient(),
            sdl_client=OfflineSdlClient(),
        )
    }
    result = {r: [built[a] for a in sorted(found[r]) if a in built] for r in roots}
    return Partial(result, tuple(sorted(missing))) if partial else result

    self, accession: str, *, partial: bool = False
) -> list[Experiment] | Partial[list[Experiment]]:
    """Return the SRA experiments under one accession, sorted, with no network call.

    The store twin of :func:`labdata.experiments_for`: the same ``Experiment`` type,
    built from the stored package XML by the same parser. Their properties, and their
    runs', never call NCBI; ``Run.files`` and ``Run.original_files`` raise instead.
    With ``partial=True`` it returns a ``Partial`` of that list and the missing
    accessions.

    Raises
    ------
    AccessionError
        If the accession is malformed.
    NotFound
        If no snapshot lists the accession.
    NotMirrored
        If the accession, or a record under it, is not held (unless ``partial``).
    """
    key = _norm(accession)
    if partial:
        walk = self.experiments_for_many([accession], partial=True)
        return Partial(walk.held[key], walk.missing)
    return self.experiments_for_many([accession])[key]

def table(self, type: str, fields: Sequence[str], where: str | None = None) -> pa.Table:
    """Return one record type as a ``pyarrow.Table``, sorted by accession, in one call.

    The only call that imports pyarrow.

    Parameters
    ----------
    type : str
        A record type, such as ``"GEO Series"`` or ``"SRA experiment"``.
    fields : sequence of str
        Raw field names. Each becomes a list column of every value, in source order.
    where : str or None
        A DuckDB condition over the columns, such as ``"published >= '2020-01-01'"``.
        It is trusted SQL from the caller, pasted into the query as written.

    Returns
    -------
    pyarrow.Table
        ``accession``, ``type``, ``status``, ``submitted``, ``updated``, ``published``,
        ``content_hash`` and ``snapshot_date``, then one column per field.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the record type is unknown, or ``where`` holds a ``;``.
    """
    if type not in _SNAPSHOT_OF:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown record type {type!r}; known: {sorted(_SNAPSHOT_OF)}")
    if where is not None and ";" in where:
        raise ValueError(f"where must be one condition, without ';': {where!r}")
    return self.reader.table(type, list(fields), where)

def open_store(root: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> Store:
    """Open the store, resolving its root without network or prompt.

    The root is the first of: the ``root`` argument, ``LABDATA_STORE``, then the per-user
    pointer file written by ``labdata store configure``. Opening writes nothing in the store.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : str or os.PathLike or None
        The store root. ``None`` falls back to the environment, then the pointer file.

    Returns
    -------
    Store
        The opened store.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreNotConfiguredError
        If no root is set anywhere.
    NotAStoreError
        If the root has no ``labdata-store.toml``.
    """
    if root is None:
        root = os.environ.get(STORE_ENV, "").strip() or _from_pointer()
    if root is None:
        raise StoreNotConfiguredError(
            f"store not configured: pass open_store(root=...), set {STORE_ENV}, "
            "or run `labdata store configure <root>`"
        )
    path = Path(root)
    return Store(root=path, settings=read_marker(path))

def read_marker(root: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the store's parsed ``labdata-store.toml``.

    Raises
    ------
    NotAStoreError
        If the root has no marker.
    """
    marker = root / MARKER
    if not marker.is_file():
        raise NotAStoreError(f"{root} is not a labdata store: it has no {MARKER}")
    with marker.open("rb") as fh:
        return tomllib.load(fh)

def init_store(root: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> Path:
    """Create the store root if missing and write its marker, ``format_version = 1``.

    The marker appears whole or not at all, and nothing else in the root is touched.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : str or os.PathLike
        The store root.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The marker written.

    Raises
    ------
    LabdataError
        If the root already has a marker.
    """
    path = Path(root)
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    marker = path / MARKER
    tmp = temp_beside(marker, "init")
    tmp.write_text(f"format_version = {FORMAT_VERSION}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        # A hard link fails if the marker exists, so two inits cannot both win.
        os.link(tmp, marker)
    except FileExistsError:
        raise LabdataError(f"{marker} already exists; this store is initialised") from None
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return marker

    """Write the per-user pointer file, which holds only the store root.

    Parameters
    ----------

pipeline ¶

Drive one round of the full run with Snakemake: fetch, pack, extract, build, prune, copy.

The DAG lives in the packaged pipeline.smk. Each step is a labdata store subcommand, so labdata owns what a step does and Snakemake owns the order and the resume: a step's marker appears only when the step exits cleanly, and a rerun starts at the first step without one. An ncbi resource caps the network steps apart from --cores, and a mem_mb resource keeps the steps that run at once inside the job's memory.

A round's markers, logs and Snakemake state sit in <root>/work/run/<round>/, where the round names the geo-series snapshot date and the sample fraction, e.g. 2026-10-14-f0.01. Every snakemake call goes through :func:_run_snakemake, the seam tests replace.

def memory_plan(total_mb: int) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Return each step's memory in MB, so the steps that can run at once fit in ``total_mb``.

    The fetch lanes, the target list and pack run beside a snapshot extract and take a small
    share each; the extract takes the rest. The build and coverage run alone with all of it.
    """
    geo, lane = total_mb // 16, total_mb // 8
    return {
        "targets": lane,
        "geo": geo,
        "eutils": lane,
        "pack": lane,
        "extract": total_mb - geo - lane,
        "build": total_mb,
        "coverage": total_mb,
        "prune": lane,
        "copy": lane,
    }

def run(
    root: Path,
    *,
    fraction: float | None = None,
    cores: int | None = None,
    ncbi: int = NCBI_STEPS,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> int:
    """Run one round: the seeded sample of ``fraction`` of the target list, or all of it.

    The round uses the newest snapshot of every source and records their dates in
    ``run.json`` in its folder. A rerun of the same round resumes at the first unfinished
    step; the fetch steps skip every item already saved, by this round or a smaller one. A
    fetch lane that left items failed runs again, and so does every step after it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    fraction : float or None
        The round's sample of the target list, in (0, 1]; ``None`` or ``1`` for all of it.
    cores : int or None
        Cores the steps may use; defaults to :func:`labdata.store._limits.default_workers`.
    ncbi : int
        Network steps that may run at once.
    verbose : bool
        Show Snakemake's and each step's output.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Snakemake's exit code: ``0`` when every step finished, coverage included.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If a snapshot source has no snapshot.
    ValueError
        If the fraction is not in (0, 1].
    """
    fraction = targets.check_fraction(fraction)
    store = open_store(root)
    root = store.root
    dates = {source: snapshots.snapshot(root, source).date for source in extract.SOURCES}
    geo_date = dates[snapshots.GEO_SERIES]
    work = round_dir(root, geo_date, fraction)
    work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # --forcerun reruns a rule and every rule after it, even where their markers exist.
    rerun = []
    for lane, rule in LANES.items():
        if (work / f"{lane}.failed").is_file():
            logger.info("the %s lane left items failed last time; it runs again", lane)
            rerun.append(rule)
    cores = cores or _limits.default_workers()
    memory = int(_limits.allocation_mb() * STEPS_SHARE)
    labdata = f"{shlex.quote(sys.executable)} -m labdata"
    config = {
        "labdata": labdata,
        "root": str(root),
        "fraction": "" if fraction is None else repr(fraction),
        "snapshots": dates,
        "targets": str(targets.list_path(root, geo_date, fraction)),
        "copy": bool(store.settings.get(gcs.COPY_TO_KEY)),
        "mem_mb": memory_plan(memory),
    }
    config_path = work / "config.json"
    config_path.write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    started = dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    record = {"fraction": fraction, "snapshots": dates, "started": started}
    (work / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    logger.info("round %s: snapshots %s", work.name, dates)
    argv = [
        "--snakefile",
        str(_snakefile()),
        "--directory",
        str(work),
        "--cores",
        str(cores),
        "--resources",
        f"ncbi={ncbi}",
        f"mem_mb={memory}",
        "--configfile",
        str(config_path),
        "--printshellcmds",
        *RESILIENCE_FLAGS,
        *(["--forcerun", *rerun] if rerun else []),
    ]
    return _run_snakemake(argv, verbose=verbose)

targets ¶

The target Series list: the sequencing Series of one dated geo-series snapshot.

A Series is a target when its esummary gdstype names high-throughput sequencing, whatever its SOFT !Series_type says. The list is streamed from the snapshot into <root>/work/targets/geo-series-<date>.parquet once per snapshot date; a build or a coverage check remakes it when missing.

A round of the full run works through a seeded sample of the list. A Series is in the sample of fraction f when its seeded hash falls below f, so a smaller round's sample lies inside every larger one's, whatever the list's order or length.

def in_sample(accession: str, fraction: float) -> bool:
    """Return whether a Series is in the seeded sample of ``fraction`` of the target list.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> in_sample("GSE1", 1.0)
    True
    """
    digest = hashlib.blake2b(f"{SEED}:{accession}".encode(), digest_size=8).digest()
    return int.from_bytes(digest) < fraction * 2**64

def check_fraction(fraction: float | None) -> float | None:
    """Return ``fraction``, or ``None`` for the whole list (``None`` or ``1``).

    if not 0 < fraction < 1:

def target_list(root: Path, date: str | None = None, fraction: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Return the target Series list of one ``geo-series`` snapshot, writing it if missing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    date : str or None
        The snapshot date; defaults to the newest snapshot.
    fraction : float or None
        A round's seeded sample of the list (see :func:`in_sample`); ``None`` or ``1`` for all.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        A Parquet file of ``accession``, ``gdstype`` and ``bioproject`` (empty when the
        snapshot gives none), one row per target Series, in snapshot order.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If the store has no such snapshot.
    ValueError
        If the fraction is not in (0, 1].
    """
    fraction = check_fraction(fraction)
    snap = snapshots.snapshot(root, snapshots.GEO_SERIES, date)
    out = list_path(root, snap.date, fraction)
    if out.is_file():
        return out
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = temp_beside(out)
    try:
        with pq.ParquetWriter(tmp, SCHEMA) as writer:
            batch: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
            for row in _targets(snap.path):
                if fraction is not None and not in_sample(row[0], fraction):
                    continue
                batch.append(row)
                if len(batch) == _BATCH:
                    writer.write_table(_table(batch))
                    batch = []
            writer.write_table(_table(batch))
        tmp.replace(out)
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return out

def summary_links(path: Path) -> Iterator[LinkRow]:
    """Yield each target Series' snapshot BioProject as a ``GEO summary`` link, batch by batch.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path
        A target Series list from :func:`target_list`.
    """
    for batch in pq.ParquetFile(path).iter_batches(columns=["accession", "bioproject"]):
        for gse, prj in zip(*batch.to_pydict().values(), strict=True):
            if prj:
                yield LinkRow(gse, prj, "BioProject", GEO_SUMMARY)

geo_lane ¶

The GEO lane: family SOFT and filelist.txt of every target Series, from GEO's site.

Each Series' family SOFT is streamed over a few kept-open HTTPS connections with its sample and platform data tables stripped on the way; the stored text starts with the original file's size and sha256. Every Series and SubSeries met is fetched whatever its SOFT type. A SOFT 404 or exhausted retries is saved as a raw/geo-gaps/ row. A fetch-failed Series is asked once more before the lane ends, and again on the next run; a soft-missing one is not. Each held Series then gets its filelist.txt, a 404 saved as an empty text. Results are written as parts for the pack step; a saved item makes no request.

def run(
    root: Path,
    series: Iterable[str],
    *,
    client: EntrezClient,
    date: str | None = None,
    connections: int = CONNECTIONS,
) -> LaneReport:
    """Fetch the family SOFT of each Series and its SubSeries, then each held one's filelist.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root; parts go under ``work/parts/``.
    series : iterable of str
        The target Series.
    client : EntrezClient
        The NCBI seam; only its ``stream`` is used.
    date : str or None
        The fetch date to record; defaults to today's UTC date.
    connections : int
        Connections kept open; halved on HTTP 429, 503 or repeated timeouts.

    Returns
    -------
    LaneReport
        Counts over every Series met, saved before this run or now.
    """
    date = date or dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).date().isoformat()
    todo = sorted({s.strip().upper() for s in series})
    seen: set[str] = set()
    retried = False
    with _Pool(client, connections) as pool:
        rounds = 0
        while todo:
            rounds += 1
            seen |= set(todo)
            what = "retry of failed" if retried else f"round {rounds}"
            _fetch_soft(root, pool, todo, date, f"Series SOFT, {what}")
            todo = sorted(_named_subseries(root, set(todo)) - seen)
            if not todo and not retried:
                retried = True
                todo = sorted(_failed(root, seen - _soft_held(root, seen)))
        held = sorted(_soft_held(root, seen))
        _fetch_filelists(root, pool, held, date)
        if len(_accessions(root, raw.GEO_FILELIST, set(held))) < len(held):
            _fetch_filelists(root, pool, held, date)
    reasons = Counter(text.split("\n", 1)[0] for text in _gap_texts(root, seen - set(held)))
    return LaneReport(
        held=len(held),
        soft_missing=reasons[gaps.SOFT_MISSING],
        fetch_failed=reasons[gaps.FETCH_FAILED],
        filelists=len(_accessions(root, raw.GEO_FILELIST, set(held))),
    )

def original(text: str) -> tuple[int, str] | None:
    """Return the size and sha256 of the file a stored SOFT text was stripped from.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of (int, str) or None
        The original's bytes and hex sha256, or ``None`` for a text stored unstripped.
    """
    head = text.split("\n", 2)
    if len(head) < 3 or not head[0].startswith(SIZE_LINE) or not head[1].startswith(SHA256_LINE):
        return None
    return int(head[0].removeprefix(SIZE_LINE)), head[1].removeprefix(SHA256_LINE)

def strip_soft(chunks: Iterable[bytes]) -> str:
    """Return family SOFT without its sample and platform data tables, size and sha256 first.

    Each table goes with its begin and end lines; every other line is kept as served.
    """
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    size = 0
    kept: list[bytes] = []
    inside = False
    carry = b""
    for chunk in itertools.chain(chunks, [None]):
        if chunk is None:
            block, carry = carry, b""
        else:
            digest.update(chunk)
            size += len(chunk)
            cut = chunk.rfind(b"\n") + 1
            if not cut:
                carry += chunk
                continue
            block, carry = carry + chunk[:cut], chunk[cut:]
        at = 0
        while at < len(block):
            match = (_TABLE_END if inside else _TABLE_BEGIN).search(block, at)
            if not inside:
                kept.append(block[at : match.start() if match else len(block)])
            if not match:
                break
            at = match.end() if inside else match.start()
            inside = not inside
    body = b"".join(kept).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    return f"{SIZE_LINE}{size}\n{SHA256_LINE}{digest.hexdigest()}\n{body}"

eutils ¶

The E-utilities lane: the SRA EXPERIMENT_PACKAGE of every GEO-linked experiment.

The experiment list is the union of the SRX accessions in saved SOFT !Sample_relation lines and the SRA_Accessions.tab experiments with Center=GEO and a GSM alias, each with its tab status. Packages come from efetch in batches, several calls in flight under the client's shared rate cap. Each bucket's piece is split into parts of a few thousand experiments, so a preempted run loses at most a few open parts. An experiment NCBI serves no package for is saved as an sra-xml row with empty text, which the build lists in its notes. Each run also asks again for a saved package that is empty while the tab says live, or that the current build notes as not well-formed. Every step streams: the tab, the SOFT text and the list are read in chunks and spilled to Parquet under work/eutils/.

reasked counts saved bad packages asked for again, recovered those that came back good. A bad saved package NCBI again serves none for is kept as saved and is not in missing.

def experiment_list(
    root: Path, *, date: str | None = None, series: Iterable[str] | None = None
) -> Path:
    """Write the lane's experiment list and return its path.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    date : str or None
        The ``SRA_Accessions.tab`` snapshot date; defaults to the newest.
    series : iterable of str or None
        Only these GEO Series' experiments: SOFT relations of these Series, and tab rows
        whose GSM the newest ``geo-series`` snapshot lists under one of them. Every
        Series by default.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        ``work/eutils/experiments-<date>.parquet``: ``accession`` and ``status`` (empty when
        the tab does not list it), one row per experiment, in bucket order. It is rewritten
        on every call, as the saved SOFT may have grown.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If the store has no such snapshot.
    """
    snap = snapshots.snapshot(root, snapshots.SRA_ACCESSIONS, date)
    folder = root / "work" / "eutils"
    tab = _tab_experiments(snap, folder / f"tab-{snap.date}.parquet")
    wanted = None if series is None else set(series)
    soft = _soft_experiments(root, folder / "soft.parquet", wanted)
    geo = "geo"
    if wanted is not None:
        samples = _samples(root, folder / "samples.parquet", wanted)
        geo = f"geo AND gsm IN (SELECT accession FROM read_parquet('{samples}'))"
    out = list_path(root, snap.date)
    tmp = temp_beside(out)
    try:
        with extract.connect(root) as con:
            con.execute(
                f"""
                COPY (
                  WITH tab AS (
                    SELECT accession, any_value(status) AS status, bool_or({geo}) AS geo
                    FROM read_parquet('{tab}') GROUP BY accession
                  ),
                  wanted AS (
                    SELECT accession FROM tab WHERE geo
                    UNION SELECT accession FROM read_parquet('{soft}')
                  )
                  SELECT w.accession, coalesce(t.status, '') AS status
                  FROM wanted w LEFT JOIN tab t USING (accession)
                  WHERE regexp_matches(w.accession, '^[A-Z]+[0-9]+$')
                  ORDER BY regexp_extract(w.accession, '^[A-Z]+'), length(w.accession),
                           w.accession
                ) TO '{tmp}' (FORMAT parquet)
                """
            )
        tmp.replace(out)
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return out

def fetch_packages(
    root: Path,
    experiments: Path,
    *,
    client: EntrezClient,
    date: str,
    batch: int = BATCH,
    inflight: int = INFLIGHT,
    part_size: int = EXPERIMENTS_PER_PART,
    log_every: float = EVERY,
) -> LaneReport:
    """Fetch the package of every listed experiment no part or raw bucket holds yet.

    Calls finish in any order: a slow call holds back only its own part, while at most
    :data:`OPEN_PARTS` parts are open at once.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    experiments : pathlib.Path
        The list from :func:`experiment_list`.
    client : EntrezClient
        The Entrez seam; its limiter sets the rate.
    date : str
        The fetch date recorded on every row.
    batch, inflight, part_size : int
        Experiments per call, calls in flight, experiments per part.
    log_every : float
        Seconds between progress lines.

    Returns
    -------
    LaneReport
        Counts for this run. An experiment whose call failed is asked once more before the
        lane ends; if that fails too it is not saved, so the next run asks for it again. A new
        one NCBI has no package for is saved with an empty text and counted in ``missing``.
        Saved bad packages are asked again: ``reasked`` counts them, ``recovered`` those that
        came back good and replace the saved copy.
    """
    sizes = (batch, inflight, part_size)
    noted = gaps.noted(root, gaps.UNPARSABLE_PACKAGE)
    first, settled = _fetch_once(root, experiments, client, date, sizes, log_every, noted, set())
    report = first
    if first.failed:
        logger.info("asking again for the %d experiments whose calls failed", first.failed)
        last, _ = _fetch_once(root, experiments, client, date, sizes, log_every, noted, settled)
        report = LaneReport(
            first.fetched + last.fetched,
            first.missing + last.missing,
            last.failed,
            len(settled) + last.reasked,
            first.recovered + last.recovered,
        )
    logger.info(
        "asked again for %d saved bad packages; %d came back good",
        report.reasked,
        report.recovered,
    )
    return report

raw ¶

Raw text in buckets: fetch lanes write parts under work/parts/, pack merges them.

A raw row is accession, raw_text, hash and fetch_date. A source's rows sit in raw/<source>/<bucket>.parquet, a bucket being a range of :data:WIDTHS accession numbers.

A fetch lane splits its work into :class:Piece s, one per bucket, and writes each finished piece as one part file that appears by a rename. A rerun skips every accession a part or a raw bucket already holds, so a saved piece makes no request. Only :mod:labdata.store.pack writes raw/. Writer side only, so pyarrow is imported here freely.

def bucket_of(source: str, accession: str) -> str:
    """Return the bucket an accession's rows go in within one source.

    The bucket keeps the accession's prefix and its number with the last digits of the
    source's width written ``n``: at width 10,000, ``GSE246310`` -> ``GSE24nnnn``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the accession is not letters then digits.
    KeyError
        If the source has no width in :data:`WIDTHS`.
    """
    digits = len(str(WIDTHS[source])) - 1
    if match := _ACCESSION.match(accession):
        return f"{match[1]}{match[2][:-digits]}{'n' * digits}"
    raise ValueError(f"no raw bucket for {accession!r}")

def part_files(root: Path, source: str) -> list[Path]:
    """Return a source's finished part files, oldest first."""
    folder = parts_dir(root, source)
    if not folder.is_dir():
        return []
    files = [p for p in folder.glob("*.parquet") if not p.name.startswith(".")]
    return sorted(files, key=lambda p: (p.stat().st_mtime_ns, p.name))

def pieces(root: Path, source: str, accessions: Iterable[str]) -> list[Piece]:
    """Split accessions into pieces, one per bucket, leaving out every saved accession.

    An accession is saved when a raw bucket row or a part holds it, or a part's piece asked
    for it and got no row. A bucket with nothing left to fetch yields no piece.
    """
    by_bucket: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    for accession in accessions:
        by_bucket[bucket_of(source, accession)].add(accession)
    done = _done(root, source, set(by_bucket))
    return [
        Piece(source, bucket, tuple(sorted(wanted - done[bucket])))
        for bucket, wanted in sorted(by_bucket.items())
        if wanted - done[bucket]
    ]

    date: str,
    *,

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    source : str
        The raw folder name, e.g. ``"sra-xml"``.
    accessions : iterable of str
        Every accession the lane wants saved.
    get : callable
        Takes one piece's accessions and yields ``(accession, raw_text)`` pairs; it may
        stream, as rows are spilled to the part in chunks.
    date : str
        The fetch date recorded on every row.
    remember_misses : bool
        Whether an accession ``get`` gave no row for counts as saved until the next pack.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The parts written; a saved piece writes none and makes no call to ``get``.
    """
    return [
        write_part(
            root,
            piece,
            (RawRow(a, text, date) for a, text in get(list(piece.todo))),
            record_asked=remember_misses,
        )
        for piece in pieces(root, source, accessions)
    ]

def write_part(
    root: Path,
    piece: Piece,
    rows: Iterable[RawRow],
    *,
    record_asked: bool = True,
    chunk_bytes: int = SORT_CHUNK_BYTES,
) -> Path:
    """Write one piece's rows as a part file, chunk by chunk, renamed into place when whole.

    Each chunk is sorted by accession and written as one row group, so memory holds one
    chunk. With ``record_asked``, the part records ``piece.todo`` as asked, so an accession
    with no row is not fetched again before the next pack.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a row belongs to another bucket.
    """
    folder = parts_dir(root, piece.source)
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tag = hashlib.sha256("\n".join(piece.todo).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    path = folder / f"{piece.bucket}.{tag}.parquet"

    def checked() -> Iterator[RawRow]:
        for row in rows:
            if bucket_of(piece.source, row.accession) != piece.bucket:
                raise ValueError(f"{row.accession} is not in bucket {piece.bucket}")
            yield row

    listed = "\n".join(piece.todo) if record_asked else ""
    schema = SCHEMA.with_metadata({ASKED_KEY: listed.encode()})
    write_sorted_runs(path, checked(), schema, chunk_bytes=chunk_bytes)
    return path

def write_sorted_runs(
    path: Path, rows: Iterable[RawRow], schema: pa.Schema, *, chunk_bytes: int = SORT_CHUNK_BYTES
) -> None:
    """Write rows to ``path`` one chunk at a time, each chunk sorted by accession.

    A chunk is written as :data:`GROUPS_PER_CHUNK` row groups, so a reader merging many
    sorted runs holds one small row group of each. The file appears by a rename once whole.
    Rows already in order make a sorted file.
    """
    tmp = writer_temp(path)
    try:
        with pq.ParquetWriter(tmp, schema) as writer:
            chunk: list[RawRow] = []
            size = 0
            for row in rows:
                chunk.append(row)
                size += len(row.raw_text)
                if size >= chunk_bytes or len(chunk) >= SORT_CHUNK_ROWS:
                    _write_chunk(writer, chunk, schema, chunk_bytes)
                    chunk, size = [], 0
            if chunk:
                _write_chunk(writer, chunk, schema, chunk_bytes)
        tmp.replace(path)
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)

def writer_temp(path: Path) -> Path:
    """Return a hidden temporary path beside ``path``, unique to this process and thread."""

def saved(root: Path, source: str, accessions: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return the saved raw text of those ``accessions`` that have a row, in raw or a part.

    A part's row wins over a raw bucket's, and a newer part's over an older one's.
    """
    wanted = set(accessions)
    buckets = {bucket_of(source, a) for a in wanted}
    paths = [root / "raw" / source / f"{bucket}.parquet" for bucket in sorted(buckets)]
    paths += [p for p in part_files(root, source) if part_bucket(p) in buckets]
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for path in paths:
        out |= {row.accession: row.raw_text for row in _read(path) if row.accession in wanted}
    return out

def read_rows(root: Path, source: str) -> list[RawRow]:
    """Return every raw row of one source, sorted by accession."""
    folder = root / "raw" / source
    rows = [row for path in sorted(folder.glob("*.parquet")) for row in _read(path)]
    return sorted(rows, key=_key)

pack ¶

Pack: merge parts into raw/<source>/<bucket>.parquet, the only writer of raw/.

A bucket is rewritten whole by a k-way merge of its sorted inputs, read a few rows at a time and written a chunk at a time, so memory holds a chunk, never a bucket or a source. For one accession, a part's row replaces the bucket's, and a newer part's an older one's. A bucket file named for another width is first split into parts, so a width change repacks the same rows.

def pack(
    root: Path, sources: Iterable[str] | None = None, *, chunk_bytes: int = raw.SORT_CHUNK_BYTES
) -> list[Path]:
    """Merge every source's parts into its raw buckets and document the folders changed.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    sources : iterable of str or None
        The raw folders to pack; defaults to every source with parts or a bucket file.
    chunk_bytes : int
        Raw text held before a row group is written.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The bucket files rewritten.
    """
    if sources is None:
        found = {p.name for p in (root / "work" / "parts").glob("*") if p.is_dir()}
        found |= {p.name for p in (root / "raw").glob("*") if p.is_dir()}
        sources = sorted(found)
    written: list[Path] = []
    for source in sources:
        done = _pack_source(root, source, chunk_bytes)
        written += done
        if done:
            provenance.document_raw(root, source)
    return written

def write_rows(root: Path, source: str, rows: list[RawRow]) -> list[Path]:
    """Save rows through parts and pack them: a row replaces any row of its accession.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The bucket files rewritten.
    """
    by_bucket: dict[str, list[RawRow]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        by_bucket[raw.bucket_of(source, row.accession)].append(row)
    for bucket, chunk in sorted(by_bucket.items()):
        piece = raw.Piece(source, bucket, tuple(sorted({row.accession for row in chunk})))
        raw.write_part(root, piece, chunk)
    return pack(root, [source])

gaps ¶

Gaps, build notes and the coverage check of the target Series list.

The GEO fetch records each target Series it could not save as a raw/geo-gaps/ row made by :func:gap_row. The build writes gaps.parquet: every target Series it does not hold, with the recorded reason, or unexplained when none was recorded. A Series held later leaves the gaps whatever its old row says. Everything here reads and writes Parquet files through DuckDB, so memory is bounded by DuckDB's cap, not by the store.

def gap_row(series: str, reason: str, fetch_date: str, detail: str = "") -> raw.RawRow:
    """Return the ``raw/geo-gaps/`` row recording why the fetch could not save a Series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series : str
        The target Series.
    reason : str
        ``SOFT_MISSING`` or ``FETCH_FAILED``.
    fetch_date : str
        The fetch date.
    detail : str
        One line, such as the last error; optional.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the reason is not a recordable one.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> gap_row("GSE1", SOFT_MISSING, "2026-10-14").raw_text
    'soft-missing'
    """
    if reason not in (SOFT_MISSING, FETCH_FAILED):
        raise ValueError(f"not a recordable gap reason: {reason!r}")
    line = " ".join(detail.split())
    return raw.RawRow(series, f"{reason}\n{line}" if line else reason, fetch_date)

def write_gaps(
    root: Path, build_dir: Path, target_list: Path, date: str, fraction: float | None = None
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Write ``gaps.parquet`` from the target list, ``holdings.parquet`` and ``raw/geo-gaps/``.

    ``fraction`` names the round's sample the target list is, so coverage re-reads the same.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``snapshot_date``, ``target`` and ``held`` counts, and ``gaps``: the count by reason,
        every reason listed; ``fraction`` too for a round's sample.
    """
    out = GAPS.path(build_dir)
    metadata = {DATE_KEY: date}
    if fraction is not None:
        metadata[FRACTION_KEY] = repr(fraction)
    reasons = ", ".join(sql_string(r) for r in REASONS[:-1])
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        layout.write(
            con,
            GAPS,
            out,
            f"""WITH g AS ({_gap_rows(root)})
            SELECT t.accession,
              CASE WHEN g.reason IN ({reasons}) THEN g.reason ELSE '{UNEXPLAINED}' END
                AS reason,
              CASE WHEN g.reason IS NULL OR g.reason IN ({reasons}) THEN g.detail
                ELSE 'recorded reason: ' || g.reason END AS detail
            FROM (SELECT DISTINCT accession FROM {_read(target_list)}) t
            LEFT JOIN g USING (accession)
            WHERE t.accession NOT IN ({_held_series(build_dir)})""",
            metadata,
        )
        counts = dict(
            con.execute(f"SELECT reason, count(*) FROM {_read(out)} GROUP BY 1").fetchall()
        )
        target = _count(con, f"SELECT count(DISTINCT accession) FROM {_read(target_list)}")
    by_reason = {reason: int(counts.get(reason, 0)) for reason in REASONS}
    summary: dict[str, object] = {"snapshot_date": date}
    if fraction is not None:
        summary["fraction"] = fraction
    return summary | {
        "target": target,
        "held": target - sum(by_reason.values()),
        "gaps": by_reason,
    }

def write_notes(
    root: Path,
    build_dir: Path,
    target_list: Path,
    extra: Iterable[Note] = (),
    experiments: Path | None = None,
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Write ``notes.parquet``: type disagreements, failed package fetches, then ``extra``.

    A failed package fetch is an experiment on the E-utilities lane's list ``experiments``
    that ``raw/sra-xml/`` does not hold.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to int
        The note count by kind.
    """
    out = NOTES.path(build_dir)
    series = records_path(build_dir, "GEO Series")
    rows = list(extra)
    extra_table = pa.table(
        {
            "accession": [n.accession for n in rows],
            "kind": [n.kind for n in rows],
            "detail": [n.detail for n in rows],
        },
        schema=NOTES.schema(),
    )
    disagree = (
        f"""SELECT t.accession, '{TYPE_DISAGREES}' AS kind,
              'snapshot: ' || t.gdstype || ' | SOFT: ' || coalesce(s.types, 'no type') AS detail
            FROM {_read(target_list)} t
            JOIN (SELECT accession FROM {_read(series)}) r USING (accession)
            LEFT JOIN (
              SELECT accession, string_agg(DISTINCT f.value, '; ' ORDER BY f.value) AS types,
                bool_or(contains(lower(f.value), {sql_string(targets.SEQUENCING)}))
                  AS sequencing
              FROM (SELECT accession, unnest(fields) AS f FROM {_read(series)})
              WHERE f.name = 'Series_type' GROUP BY accession
            ) s USING (accession)
            WHERE NOT coalesce(s.sequencing, false)"""
        if series.is_file()
        else "SELECT * FROM extra WHERE false"
    )
    unfetched = "SELECT * FROM extra WHERE false"
    saved = root / "raw" / raw.SRA_XML
    if experiments is not None and experiments.is_file():
        held = (
            f"SELECT accession FROM {_read(saved / '*.parquet')}"
            if any(saved.glob("*.parquet"))
            else "SELECT NULL::VARCHAR AS accession WHERE false"
        )
        unfetched = (
            f"SELECT accession, '{PACKAGE_FETCH_FAILED}' AS kind, "
            f"'no package saved; a rerun asks again' AS detail FROM {_read(experiments)} "
            f"WHERE accession NOT IN ({held})"
        )
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        con.register("extra", extra_table)
        layout.write(
            con, NOTES, out, f"{disagree} UNION ALL {unfetched} UNION ALL SELECT * FROM extra"
        )
        counts = con.execute(f"SELECT kind, count(*) FROM {_read(out)} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1")
        return {str(kind): int(n) for kind, n in counts.fetchall()}

def noted(root: Path, kind: str) -> set[str]:
    """Return the accessions the current build notes as ``kind``; none before a first build."""
    if current_build(root) is None:
        return set()
    notes = NOTES.path(current_path(root))
    if not notes.is_file():
        return set()
    table = pq.read_table(notes, columns=["accession"], filters=[("kind", "==", kind)])
    return set(table.column(0).to_pylist())

def coverage(root: Path, build: BuildReader) -> Coverage:
    """Check one build against the target list of the snapshot its gaps were made from.

    The target list is re-read from the snapshot, so a stale or partial ``gaps.parquet``
    fails rather than agreeing with itself. A round's build is checked against its sample.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If the build has no ``gaps.parquet`` or its snapshot is gone.
    """
    gaps_file = GAPS.path(build.path)
    if not gaps_file.is_file():
        raise StoreBuildError(f"{build.path} has no {GAPS}; rebuild with `labdata store build`")
    meta = pq.read_metadata(gaps_file).metadata or {}
    date = meta[DATE_KEY.encode()].decode()
    fraction = meta.get(FRACTION_KEY.encode())
    target_list = targets.target_list(root, date, None if fraction is None else float(fraction))
    with extract.connect(root) as con:
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW t AS SELECT DISTINCT accession FROM {_read(target_list)}")
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW h AS {_held_series(build.path)}")
        con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW g AS SELECT accession, reason, detail FROM {_read(gaps_file)}")
        target = _count(con, "SELECT count(*) FROM t")
        held = _count(con, "SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE accession IN (SELECT accession FROM h)")
        by_reason = dict(con.execute("SELECT reason, count(*) FROM g GROUP BY 1").fetchall())
        problems = f"""
            SELECT accession, 'not held and no gap row' FROM t
              WHERE accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM h)
              AND accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM g)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, 'gap row for a held Series' FROM g
              WHERE accession IN (SELECT accession FROM h)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, 'gap row for a Series not on the target list' FROM g
              WHERE accession NOT IN (SELECT accession FROM t)
            UNION ALL SELECT accession, '{UNEXPLAINED}' || coalesce(': ' || detail, '') FROM g
              WHERE reason = '{UNEXPLAINED}'"""
        failures = _count(con, f"SELECT count(*) FROM ({problems})")
        failing = con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM ({problems}) ORDER BY 1, 2 LIMIT {NAMED}").fetchall()
        notes = NOTES.path(build.path)
        failed_experiments = (
            _count(
                con,
                f"SELECT count(*) FROM {_read(notes)} WHERE kind = '{PACKAGE_FETCH_FAILED}'",
            )
            if notes.is_file()
            else 0
        )
    return Coverage(
        snapshot_date=date,
        target=target,
        held=held,
        gaps={reason: int(by_reason.get(reason, 0)) for reason in (*REASONS, *by_reason)},
        failing=tuple((str(a), str(p)) for a, p in failing),
        failures=failures,
        failed_experiments=failed_experiments,
    )

prune ¶

Delete the builds and snapshots the store no longer reads, after a grace period.

A non-current build goes once the store switched away from it more than the grace period ago, GRACE by default. A snapshot goes once it is older than the one the current build reads and every build that read it went out of use more than the grace period ago; its extract parts under work/ go with it. A snapshot newer than the current build's is waiting for the next build and stays. Neither the current build nor what it reads is ever deleted.

def prune(
    root: Path, *, now: dt.datetime | None = None, grace: dt.timedelta = GRACE
) -> PruneReport:
    """Delete old builds and unread snapshots, keeping everything inside the grace period.

    A build switched away from before switch times were recorded counts as switched away
    when the current build was switched to. After deleting anything, it rewrites the root
    ``README.md`` so its sizes stay current.

    Parameters
    ----------
    root : pathlib.Path
        The store root.
    now : datetime.datetime or None
        The time to measure the grace period from; defaults to the current UTC time.
    grace : datetime.timedelta
        How long a build stays after the store switched away from it: ``GRACE``, 24 hours,
        by default. Zero deletes at once.

    Returns
    -------
    PruneReport
        The folders deleted.

    Raises
    ------
    StoreBuildError
        If a build, prune or copy of this store is running.
    """
    now = now or dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC)
    with build_lock(root):
        marker = root / MARKER
        settings = read_marker(root)
        current = settings.get(BUILD_KEY)
        if not current:
            return PruneReport()
        switched = _time(settings.get(SWITCHED_KEY)) or dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(
            marker.stat().st_mtime, dt.UTC
        )
        away: dict[str, str] = settings.get(SWITCHED_AWAY_KEY, {})
        builds = build_folders(root)
        reads = {b.name: _reads(b) for b in builds}
        unused_since = {
            b.name: _time(away.get(b.name)) or switched for b in builds if b.name != current
        }
        old = [build_path(root, name) for name, t in unused_since.items() if now - t > grace]
        latest = dict(reads.get(str(current), set()))
        snaps = []
        for folder in sorted((root / "snapshots").glob("*/*")):
            source, date = folder.parent.name, folder.name
            if not (folder.is_dir() and _DATE.match(date)) or date >= latest.get(source, date):
                continue
            readers = [n for n, t in unused_since.items() if (source, date) in reads[n]]
            if now - max((unused_since[n] for n in readers), default=switched) > grace:
                snaps.append(folder)
        for folder in [*old, *snaps]:
            shutil.rmtree(folder)
        for folder in snaps:
            shutil.rmtree(
                extract.extract_dir(root, folder.parent.name, folder.name), ignore_errors=True
            )
        if any(p.name in away for p in old):
            settings[SWITCHED_AWAY_KEY] = {k: v for k, v in away.items() if not _gone(root, k)}
            write_marker(root, settings)
        if old or snaps:
            readme.try_write(root)
        return PruneReport([*old, *snaps])
